title: Genta's Certain Kill Shot
notes: case_type: attempted_murder (victim Ludger Heinen survives and reappears in Part 2's coda, cheesecake gift in hand). Recurring core-4 detective cast (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention -- Megure appears only as a throwaway fat-joke reference, not as a case participant. The rest of the Detective Boys (Genta, Ayumi, Mitsuhiko, Haibara), Professor Agasa, and Officer Takagi are all included since they are named, present, and functionally load-bearing (Genta is both the accidental witness and the accusation target; Takagi runs the suspect roundup and later confirms the motive by phone; Agasa drives, buys the cake, and calls the ambulance). No `event` node type: crime actions are direct typed edges between the real people/objects/locations. The old low-fidelity `cases/` file's culprit (Kanji Kojima), victim (Ludger Heinen), suspect trio, and weapon (metal rod / steel pipe) all check out against the transcript -- unlike several other rebuilt episodes, this one's wiki-derived hypothesis was correct on the core facts. What the old file missed entirely: the linguistic double-meaning clue ('Elf' = German for eleven, matching Kojima's jersey number 11, vs. English for a mischievous fairy, the reason Ludger pointed at Genta first) that is the episode's actual centerpiece deduction; the two red-herring suspects' accusations were pure wordplay (name-sound-alikes and a kanji anagram), not motive-based, so no fabricated `has_motive_against` edges were added for them -- captured instead as `accuses` edges tagged red_herring. Old file also had Genta accused via `knows` edges and a generic robbery-attempt event; here that's decomposed into `assaults`, `steals`, `wields`, and the three clue nodes that actually break the case (the elf/eleven pun, the alibi-knowledge contradiction, and the horse-race name test).

clues.desc: Ludger's dying word 'El-' has two readings: English 'elf' (a mischievous fairy, why he pointed at Genta first) and German 'elf' (eleven, matching the number 11 on Kojima's jersey) -- one syllable encoding two separate hints at once.
Kojima knows Genta was first to find Ludger's body, a detail the police never told him and he could not have learned while genuinely isolated in his car as claimed.
Kojima cannot name the horse that won today's main race, despite claiming to have been listening to it live during the exact window of the attack.
